findings.body: The `shorten` doc says the result is at most `limit` characters, and `shorten` is used for a GitHub check-run title with a hard cap. When the first `limit` characters contain no space, the `None` branch returns `head` (exactly `limit` characters) plus `…`, so the result is `limit + 1` characters and can exceed the cap. Reserve room for the ellipsis, e.g. take only `limit - 1` characters when adding it, or document that the ellipsis may make the result `limit + 1`.
findings.title: Cap `shorten` output at `limit` when no space exists

value.summary: The change adds string shortening and first-sentence helpers with tests. One off-by-one in the no-space branch of `shorten` can make the result exceed the promised limit; otherwise the code looks sound.
